BBC News — "One dead and five missing after explosion destroys building close to Acropolis in Athens" — 26 Sep 2026, 09:33 BST

At least one person has died and five more are missing after an explosion destroyed a building in the historic centre of Athens. The blast happened in the Plaka area, close to tourist sites such as the Acropolis, with local media reporting the building housed a holiday rental.
Four American tourists, one British national and a Greek national are said to be the people involved - though that has not been confirmed by authorities.
A gas leak is suspected as the cause. The body of a woman was found on Saturday morning, with the search ongoing. The tourists were confirmed missing when they did not arrive for their flight at Athens airport, Reuters reported citing local police.
The three-storey building completely collapsed, with neighbouring buildings damaged and debris scattered across the road. Excavators and thermal imaging cameras were used to search for survivors. The explosion happened on a small road between the Acropolis and the Temple of Olympian Zeus. BBC News has contacted the UK Foreign Office.
